title: AbsorbLab
excerpt: Exact supplied finite Markov first-hit, state-aggregation and one-row probability-response laboratory. Separate a disappearing exit from its interior limit, then inspect success-conditioned state visits and every directed edge count.
headings: AbsorbLab 0.3: the last exit changes everything

title: AgentTrace - case study
excerpt: A separate exact fixed-interval retention policy under a supplied overlap cap. With one lane, two touching spans worth 6 each beat one enclosing span worth 9. Native integer min-cost flow exposes every edge, flow, canonical potential and residual reduced cost, with a matching primal/dual bound and exact zero gap.
headings: AgentTrace 0.2: keep the value, respect the overlap
Retained timing audit and original analyzer
The constraint that shaped the build
Worked example: catching a looping agent

title: AlignLab: what the comparisons leave open
excerpt: A reward optimizer can do its job while the preference data leaves its target open. AlignLab makes those two questions visible. The new inspector shows which reward ratios a comparison graph fixes, which policies still fit it, and when the supplied probabilities contradict a scalar reward model.
headings: AlignLab: what the comparisons leave open
Checks that do not just trust the producer
The original experiment is still here

title: ArgumentLab: making defense inspectable
excerpt: An exact bounded abstract-argumentation workbench. Compare all nine extension families, inspect every subset's attackers/defenders and unanswered attacks, all inclusion/range witnesses, complete three-valued labellings and the entire grounded fixed-point chain. Directed graph keeps opposite attacks and self loops visible.
headings: The edge case is part of the product
ArgumentLab: a cycle can split after a choice
ArgumentLab0.4: everyone includes it. Who defends it?

title: AttnLens
excerpt: Actual blockwise online-softmax inference on trained checkpoints: inspect running maximum, normalizer, weighted values and the full residual stack against dense causal controls. Original from-scratch training and all-head interventions remain intact. Bounded score-buffer counts are not total memory or speed claims.

title: AuctionLab: truthful alone, not protected together
excerpt: Individual honesty and coalition stability answer different questions. AuctionLab is an exact finite multiagent allocation workbench: inspect every feasible ownership vector, efficient tie, VCG externality price, report-independent bundle menu and seller-coalition deficit. Values are supplied, not learned. No actual auctions or payments.
headings: AuctionLab: truthful alone, not protected together
A coalition can be short even when no individual report helps
Every tie stays in the evidence

title: BanditLab
excerpt: Exact finite-budget Bayesian bandit planning from scratch. Independent Beta-Bernoulli arms, posterior-state Bellman backups, complete action values and ties, a fully updating greedy baseline, and an exact clairvoyant prior upper bound. Dependency-free Python 3.10+, strict JSON CLI and rational results.
headings: A lower current mean can be the better first choice
Follow a policy forward and account for every lost reward
Exact learning-state planning, not a sampled rollout
Strict inputs and exact state preflight

title: BeliefLab
excerpt: Exact rational finite-horizon planning for supplied two-hidden-state, two-observation POMDPs. Dependency-free Python 3.10+, strict JSON CLI, policy-tree witnesses, Bayesian observation branches and an exact all-belief alpha-vector envelope. No learned model or belief-grid approximation.
headings: Pay for information, then act on it
Optimized open-loop baseline and feedback advantage
Execute the policy witness as an exact probability audit
From finite plans to a discounted infinite-value bracket

title: BellmanLab
excerpt: Exact rational planning for small fully specified discounted MDPs. The model is supplied, not learned from samples. Dependency-free Python 3.10+, strict JSON CLI, three reproducible SVGs and an isolated-wheel demo.
headings: A stopping rule that checks the right quantity
Exact nested controller and adversary policy iteration

title: BetLab: sequential evidence without free restarts
excerpt: Exact sequential evidence for bounded paired model scores, with an exhaustive audit of what goes wrong when ruined tests get free restarts.
headings: BetLab: sequential evidence without free restarts

title: BisimLab
excerpt: Original finite agent-protocol equivalence inspector.
headings: BisimLab: silence can hide a choice
BisimLab0.4: the loop must stay inside

title: BoostLab: residual trees and bounded Newton leaves
excerpt: Dependency-free Python train/predict CLI and API, 36 Python tests and five Node/actual-Chrome tests, offline demo and Python 3.10-3.13 CI. Standard gradient boosting, no new theory.
headings: BoostLab: residual trees and bounded Newton leaves

title: BranchLab: always possible is not inevitable
excerpt: An explicit finite CTL inspector for branching-time reasoning about supplied models. In the default, AG EF p holds while AF p fails: a goal remains reachable everywhere, but an infinite wait is still allowed.
headings: BranchLab: always possible is not inevitable
BranchLab0.2: a fair path must meet them all

title: BuchiLab
excerpt: Tiny finite adversarial repeated-goal games with every nested greatest/least fixed-point obligation, progress rank, complete positional controller policy and reachable cyclic non-goal SCC visible. Idle can stay inside the winning region forever and still lose: rank-guided progress and per-policy audits show why.
headings: BuchiLab: a winning state is not a winning policy
Inspect the failure, not only the answer
BuchiLab0.3: the maximum that keeps returning

title: CalibrLab: confidence calibration from scratch, measured end to end
excerpt: A model can be accurate and still be wrong about how sure it is - and for anything downstream of a probability (thresholds, triage, abstention), that matters as much as accuracy.
headings: CalibrLab: confidence calibration from scratch, measured end to end
The repair, with its exact guarantee
Measured results (checked-in fixture, pinned in tests)
v0.2: inspect every score and confidence bin

title: CausalLab
excerpt: A strong association does not say what replacing a mechanism would do. Even a complete observed joint can agree under two different causal mechanisms that disagree about actions and counterfactuals. The missing information is an assumption, not a decimal place.
headings: Identical action marginals, different cross-world response types
Sharp bounds instead of choosing a coupling
More controls do not always make a valid adjustment
CausalLab: a mediator can identify an effect

title: ChainLab: sequence likelihood is not a path decoder
excerpt: Dependency-free Python, 41 Python tests and four Node/actual-Chrome tests, infer/viterbi/fit JSON CLI, reproducible SVG and Python3.10-3.13 CI. Standard HMM theory, no new method.
headings: ChainLab: sequence likelihood is not a path decoder

title: ChannelLab: same accuracy, different information
excerpt: Exact finite binary experiment comparison. A constructive state-independent garbling, or a strict two-action decision witness proving why it cannot exist. Version 0.2 adds an exact all-prior decision atlas. Dependency-free Python 3.10+ and a separate BigInt browser inspector.
headings: One task ties. The information order does not.

title: ClusterLab: shapes first, labels later
excerpt: A k-means demo can mistake arbitrary group IDs for digit recognition and monotone descent for a globally optimal fit. ClusterLab makes both errors hard to miss: forty optimization histories remain visible, learned centroids show mixed true-digit membership, and the browser runs actual editable inference rather than replaying saved predictions.
headings: v0.2: every restart, not only the winner
v0.3: uniqueness needs its own proof

title: CompileLab: one function, many shapes
excerpt: A canonical diagram still depends on its variable order. A projected model is not a sum of hidden completions. CompileLab makes both distinctions inspectable in a tiny exact Boolean knowledge-compilation workbench.
headings: Count the declared universe, not only the support
Existential projection is not arithmetic marginalization
